Vallor.

Ethical Frameworks
Best Practices
Ethical Frameworks
We will discuss 3 normative ethical frameworks of practical relevance:
Virtue Ethics
Consequentialist/Utilitarian Ethics
Deontological Ethics
We must note here that these frameworks tend to be grounded in
moral
realism
moral statements express propositions
some such propositions are true
And further,
moral objectivism
the truth value of such a proposition is independent of people’s
thought
Indeed, we must assume these stances, otherwise there is little point in
requiring an ethics module at all.
Virtue Ethics
Virtue ethics
focuses not on rules for good or bad actions, but on the qualities of
morally excellent persons (e.g. virtues). Such theories are said to be character
based…
Such theories also focus on the habits of action of virtuous persons, such as the
habit of moderation… as well as the virtue of prudence or practical wisdom…
— Vallor, 2018
3 ways this helps us understand our moral obligations:
our moral obligations derive from our basic obligation to develop our
moral character.
we can develop our moral character by continually striving to embody
the virtues of morally excellent people.
virtues like practical wisdom (good moral judgment) will lead to
flourishing both in personal life and society.
Consequentialist/Utilitarian Ethics
Consequentialist
theories… derive principles to guide moral action from the likely
consequences of those actions. The most famous form… is
Utilitarian Ethics
, which
uses the principle of the ‘greatest good’ to determine what our moral obligations are
in any given situation.
— Vallor, 2018
Utilitarians generally measure ‘good’ in terms of happiness, pleasure, or the
minimization of pain.
the action that promotes the ‘greater good’ is therefore that which
produces the greatest net sum of good in the long run.
“the ends justify the means”
However, many utilitarians argue that this does not undermine individual
rights and justice on the basis that a society that upholds such concepts
is most likely to maximize overall overall happiness.
(i have my issues with utilitarianism, but my opinions are my own)
Deontological Ethics
Deontological ethics
are rule or principle-based systems of ethics, in which one or
more rules/principles are claimed to tell us what our moral obligations are in life.
— Vallor, 2018
For example:
the Ten Commandments in Judeo-Christian thought
e.g. you shall have no other gods, honor your parents, do not murder…
filial piety in Confucian ethics
i.e. duty to respect, obey, care for parents/elders
Kant’s categorical imperative
only act in ways we would be willing to have all other persons follow at
all times.
The categorical imperative (and other deontological systems) upholds the
intrinsic value of human beings, and by extension the dignity of human
lives.
These motivate the moral obligation to treat other human beings in ways
that respect their dignity, rather than merely as means to an ends.
Think-Pair-Share
Which of these frameworks do you find personally most compelling and
why?
Best Practices
Vallor lists 12 best practices for cybersecurity ethics:
Keep Cybersecurity Ethics in the Spotlight— and Out of the
Compliance Box
ethics is not an external constraint, not simply a checkbox
what is legal may not be ethical and vice versa
Consider the Human Lives and Interests Behind the Systems
systems are meant to improve lives and protect our interests and
should handle them with appropriate care
Consider Downstream (and Upstream and Lateral) Risks in
Cybersecurity Practice
how might this device/system be used or abused?
are there risks to relying on 3rd-party components in this device/
system?
are there risks to using this device/system in conjunction with
others?
Don’t Discount Non-Technical Actors, Interests, Expectations, and
Exposures
you shouldn’t just say “skill issues” and blame the victim
Establish Chains of Ethical Responsibility and Accountability
avoid diffusion of responsibility by holding individuals accountable
for ethical implementation of security
Practice Cybersecurity Disaster Planning and Crisis Response
consider worst-case scenarios, anticipate, and mitigate consequences
“defense-in-depth”
Promote Values of Transparancy, Autonomy, and Trustworthiness
responsible disclosure and vulnerability notifications
Consider Disparate Interests, Resources, and Impacts
technologies can have asymmetric consequences that should be
anticipated
e.g. accessibility
Invite Diverse Stakeholder Input
e.g. user feedback
Design for Privacy and Security
privacy and security should be considered in early stages of design,
whether technical, social, organizational (Conway’s law)
Make Ethical Reflection & Practice Standard, Pervasive, Iterative, and
Rewarding
company culture
Model and Advocate for Ethical Cybersecurity Practice
individuals are responsible for creating/maintaining a culture
She also lists 5 practices for living well:
Practice Self-Reflection/Examination
what are the moral implications of you past actions?
how would you feel if those you respect and admire knew your
actions, choices, and thoughts?
what are your goals? what type of person you want to become?
what character traits or habits do you need to change to be that
person?
are you living up to the values you profess to yourself and others?
Look for Moral Exemplars
stop dwelling on others’ unfairness, unkindness, or incompetence
you
should
compare yourself to moral exemplars and strive to improve
Exercise Moral Imagination
imagine what it would be like to suffer the pain that our actions
might cause someone
Acknowledge Our Own Moral Strength
don’t take the easy way out if it means moral compromise
your decisions are
not
out of your hands, you
do
have moral agency.
Seek the Company of Other Moral Persons
it is much easier to do the right thing when you surround yourself
with others who also strive to do the right thing
pick your friends carefully, and be the friends others need as well
Think-Pair-Share
It’s a new semester. Are there any changes you want to make to become
more of the person you want to be?
I recommend keeping in touch and check in with one another on how you
are doing throughout the semester.
